title: "Shared physical representation"
description: "Source physical declarations and one selected-profile interpretation consumed by solver preparation."
scgsim-kind: "contract"

---

Physical classification belongs to the source author. A selected source input
uses one LayerStack assembly frame and one physical layer identity for each
physical film, shared across its Entities, polygons and child occurrences.
Placement applies once before profile interpretation. Independent stack frames
require explicit source association and are outside this contract.

A physical declaration distinguishes stack films, local films and finite
volumes. Original material, normal film thickness, attachment face, source
interval, Entity identity, polygon holes and actual body endpoints remain
source facts. A finite volume's nominal layer interval does not replace an
individual body's interval. A TSV wall's radial thickness is distinct from
its axial span. Nonmetal support locators do not become conductor films.

One neutral physical representation plan owns the selected profile, source to
effective coordinate trace, per-body representation, support projection and
complete enclosure mapping. Palace and AEDT consume that plan; backend
construction, final Nets, ports, junctions, RLC treatments and numerical
controls retain their own owners. Neither a Net, role, material name nor body
size supplies a missing physical classification.

The explicit profiles `solid`, `thin_film`, `substrate_face` and
`metal_gap_equivalent` and `route_b` describe explicit profiles. They are not aliases.
Stack-film removal occurs once per physical identity. Local-film sheet
projection uses its authored attachment face and does not remove thickness
from unrelated intervals. Retained volumes map their actual endpoints. The
complete requested source enclosure maps once, rather than reapplying source
padding around already shortened bodies in a backend.

Actual contact and host incidence remain source-bound records. Missing
qualified incidence stays missing; it does not block independent physical
lowering. A consumer requiring unavailable incidence reports that specific
limitation and does not guess from proximity, names or Net membership. Source
contact normals do not establish HFSS calculator Surface/Adjacent field-side
semantics or native electrical continuity.

Historical requests, source hashes, runtime inventories and sealed cohorts
retain their recorded interpretation. They are not a second authority for
fresh physical-source preparation. The current scope remains CONVERGING;
source preparation and offline traces do not prove native construction,
convergence or numerical accuracy.

## Typed source carrier and plan

The source owner's `LayerLevel.info["physical_layer"]` contains the serialized
neutral declaration. Preserve all original Level arguments and existing info
when adding that carrier; no solver target material is written into it.

```python
from gdsfactory.technology import LayerLevel
from scgsim.geometry.models.physical import (
    ApproximationProfile, PhysicalLayerDeclaration, PhysicalRepresentationPlan,
)
from scgsim.geometry.planning.physical import interpret_physical_geometry

declaration = PhysicalLayerDeclaration.from_payload(authored_declaration)
level = LayerLevel(
    **authored_level_arguments,  # existing source arguments, excluding info
    info={**authored_level_info, "physical_layer": declaration.to_payload()},
)
profile = ApproximationProfile("thin_film", "v1", {})
effective_input, effective_stack, plan = interpret_physical_geometry(
    normalized_source_input, source_stack, profile,
)
recorded_plan = plan.to_payload()
read_plan = PhysicalRepresentationPlan.from_payload(recorded_plan)
body = read_plan.map_body(
    declared_physical_layer_id, actual_source_interval_um, original_source_geometry,
)
```

`PhysicalLayerDeclaration` has these exact fields:

- `physical_layer_id`, `source_level_id`, `source_level_and_gds_pair` and
  `source_interval_um`: source identity, selector association and nominal span.
- `material_id` and `feature_kind`: original material and `stack_film`,
  `local_film` or `finite_volume` classification.
- `physical_dimensions`: source normal film thickness or finite-volume facts;
  radial wall thickness and axial span remain distinct.
- `source_contact_facts`: authored attachment face and available source normals.
- `actual_entity_contact_graph`: the existing authored graph, or `None` when
  unavailable. Process-connectivity descriptions are not qualified placed
  footprint/contact proof.

The plan uses schema `scgsim.geometry.physical-representation.v1`. Its tagged
payload records the explicit profile, source identity, declarations, collapse
intervals, sheet anchors, per-Entity facts and complete enclosure traces.
`context` projects those facts for shared planning; `map_body()`,
`project_support_point()` and `project_enclosure()` supply consumer projections
without a second profile interpreter.

The declaration's original `material_id` stays source identity. Native AEDT
PEC material or Perfect E/ThinConductor assignments are backend realization
and separately observed evidence; they never replace that source identity.

## Selected declarations and source incidence

A declaration catalogue is not the selected model. Consume only the physical
levels explicitly bound by the selected source; an unused catalogue film does
not create a collapse event. The selected bridge assembly now supplies qualified
M1-to-substrate, post-to-Ground and deck-to-post source incidence. Preserve those
source records and their qualified body/occurrence ownership. They establish
source incidence, not native continuity or HFSS calculator field-side proof.
Generic bridge/bump incidence still remains unavailable where it is unauthored;
missing records are neither invented nor made prerequisites for independent
physical lowering. TSV solve controls are selected by separate Human authoring
authority; this physical-source contract does not admit native jobs.

## Candidate migration

Fresh physical-source preparation consumes neutral `PhysicalLayerDeclaration`
records and an explicit `ApproximationProfile`. Fresh `aedt_modeling` metadata
and role-derived route classification are not adapters. Existing
`PhysicalLayerSpec` records retain their original serialization and coordinate
meaning for version-bound historical readers only; using them for a new
physical-source execution requires replacing them with neutral declarations.
Explicit Solid bodies without layer declarations retain their finite source
geometry through the shared identity plan, without minted physical IDs.

The selected plan's tagged payload is the current prepared physical trace.
Historical untagged traces remain readable under their original contract and
retain their original hashes; they do not authorize fresh execution.

## Palace caller profile

`ElectrostaticSim` and `EigenmodeSim` accept the typed
`approximation_profile` constructor field. `set_surface_epr()` accepts the same
keyword and replaces the selected profile when supplied; omitting it retains
the constructor-selected profile. The source-authorized bindings
identify actual normalized supporting Entities and their `lower` or `upper`
faces; they are not reconstructed from layer names, roles or equal Z values.

```python
from scgsim.geometry.models.physical import ApproximationProfile

profile = ApproximationProfile(
    name="substrate_face",
    revision="v1",
    parameters={"film_bindings": authored_film_bindings},
)
sim.set_surface_epr(
    representation="A",
    specs=authored_surface_specs,
    approximation_profile=profile,
)
```

Each `authored_film_bindings` entry is keyed by a declared physical layer ID
and contains exactly `supporting_entity_id` and `supporting_side`.
`metal_gap_equivalent` needs its two explicitly bound opposing films. Missing
bindings fail preparation with a replacement call shape before native work.
The old `route_a_thin_film` string can disclose or check the selected name; it
does not author bindings or own coordinate arithmetic. Existing Route B
selection uses the shared identity `route_b` profile when no explicit profile
is supplied. Low-level fresh `build_route_mesh()` requires preparation's
effective normalized input and representation context.

The unversioned semantic `apply_thin_film_profile`, `derive_thin_film_facts`
and `normalize_optional_profile` exports are retired in this candidate. Use
neutral declarations with `interpret_physical_layers()` or
`interpret_physical_geometry()`; original pinned source and frozen historical
artifacts retain their original code and payload identities.
